name: Walking bass
description: steady quarters or eighths stepping and leaping through the harmony with a shape of its own: `C2q D2q E2q F2q` / `C2e G2e E2e C2e G1e B1e C2e D2e`. The default in the chorale-derived and continuo textures. It should move mostly by step with an occasional leap of a fourth or fifth to a new harmony.

name: Imitation of the right hand
description: the left hand states the subject a bar or two after the right, usually at the octave or the fifth below. This is the single most characteristic Baroque texture and it is nearly absent from generated writing. If the piece has a subject, the bass must state it.

name: Running sixteenths in one voice
description: a continuous line, the same rhythmic value throughout, changing direction and register as the harmony moves: `C2s D2s E2s F2s G2s A2s B2s C3s …`. The invention and prelude engine. Its *continuity* is the point; a rest inside it is an event.

name: Broken-chord figuration
description: `C2s G2s E3s G2s C2s G2s E3s G2s`. The C major prelude shape. Note it is written as one unbroken stream, not as bass-plus- chord: the harmony is *implied* by the figure rather than stated under it.

name: Pedal point
description: the bass holds one note, usually the dominant, for four to sixteen bars while everything above changes: `G1w` repeated, or `G1w~` tied. Bach's standard preparation for a final cadence.

name: Suspension chain in an inner voice
description: a held note becomes a dissonance when the bass moves, then falls by step, then is held again. Written with ties: `F3h~ F3q E3q`. This is where Baroque expression lives, and a texture with no suspensions sounds bland however correct the chords are.

name: Two independent voices in the left hand
description: a held tenor over a moving bass, written with `//`: `C2h G2h // E3q F3q E3q D3q`. Real three- and four-voice writing needs this; a single-stream left hand cannot do it.

name: Sequence
description: the same figure transposed down a fifth or up a fourth, two to four times. `C2e E2e G2e C3e` then `F1e A1e C2e F2e` then `B1e D2e F2e B2e`. Bach's principal method of continuation, and it should be *exact* transposition, not an approximation.

name: Alberti
description: does not exist here. It is a Classical invention. Using it makes the music mid-eighteenth-century at the earliest.

name: Chordal, all voices together
description: reserved for chorale texture and for cadential arrivals: `[C2,C3,E3,G3]q`. Four real voices moving in the same rhythm, each singable.

name: The bass rests while an inner voice takes over
description: a texture change without a change of idiom. Bach thins from four voices to two and back constantly.

name: Alberti bass
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Murky bass (octave alternation)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Waltz bass (3/4, L:1/8)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Steady continuo quarters
description: `D2q A2q D3q A2q`. Root and fifth alternating, one chord per bar or per half bar. The default, and it should sound unhurried.

name: Walking eighths
description: `D2e E2e F#2e G2e A2e B2e C#3e D3e`. Drives an aria or a fast movement; mostly stepwise with an occasional leap to the next harmony.

name: Repeated notes on one pitch
description: `D2e ×8`. Insistent, and used under a sequence where the harmony above is doing the moving.

name: Dotted-rhythm bass (the French overture)
description: `D2dq D2e A2dq A2e`. Stately and ceremonial. Paired with a dotted upper part; this is the single most recognisable Handel gesture and it belongs at openings.

name: Descending tetrachord / ground bass
description: `D2h C2h Bb1h A1h`, repeated as an ostinato under changing upper material. The lament bass. Handel builds whole movements on one.

name: Octave leaps between root and its octave
description: `D2q D3q D2q D3q`. Solid and plain; gives weight without motion.

name: Sustained pedal on the dominant
description: `A1w` held for four or eight bars while the upper parts intensify. Handel's standard preparation for a final cadence and for a chorus entry.

name: Sequential descent by fifths
description: the bass falling a fourth and rising a second: `D2q G1q E2q A1q F#2q B1q`. The circle-of-fifths engine, and Handel uses it plainly and often.

name: Unison with the upper parts
description: everything on the same line, in octaves, for a declamatory opening or a sudden fortissimo. Bare and public.

name: Silence under a solo entry
description: the bass drops out entirely for a phrase so a voice or a solo instrument can be heard alone, then re-enters at the cadence. Common in the arias and almost never generated.

name: Broken octaves for agitation
description: `D2e D3e D2e D3e`. The storm and rage idiom; heavier and slower than a Classical tremolo.

name: Alberti bass
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Walking quarters through the harmony
description: `D3q A2q Bb2q F2q G2q D2q Eb2q A2q`. Steady, mostly by step or by fourth, one note per chord. The default and the sound of the style.

name: Circle of fifths, exact
description: the bass falling a fifth and rising a fourth, four to eight chords in a row: `D3q G2q C3q F2q Bb2q E2q A2q D2q`. Corelli uses longer circles than anyone before him, and the exactness is the point.

name: Suspension chain (the 7-6 or 4-3 chain)
description: the upper voices suspend in alternation while the bass walks down by step. `D3q C3q Bb2q A2q` under suspending violins. This is the single most Corellian texture there is.

name: Pedal on the dominant
description: `A2w` held for four to eight bars before a final cadence, with the violins intensifying above.

name: Repeated notes for insistence
description: `D3e ×8` under a sequential passage.

name: Bass imitating the violins
description: in the fugal movements the bass takes the subject at the octave below. The trio sonata's fast movements are usually fugal and the bass must participate.

name: Descending tetrachord ground
description: `D3h C3h Bb2h A2h`, repeated. Used for the slow movements and the chaconne-like finales.

name: Long notes under a solo passage
description: whole notes while a violin ornaments freely above. The slow-movement texture.

name: Cadential 4-3 with the bass falling a fifth
description: `A2h D2h` under a suspended fourth resolving. Every phrase ends this way; that is not monotony, it is the period's punctuation.

name: Sequences of one-bar units
description: the same bar transposed down a step or a third, three or four times. Corelli's principal method of continuation, and the transposition should be exact.

name: Silence for one beat before a cadence
description: the whole texture stops, then the cadence lands. Sparing and effective.
